maddeler.t:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *sper-der.
Latin sporta
Proto-Indo-European *-lós
Proto-Indo-European *-elós
Proto-Italic *-elos
Latin -ulus
Latin sportulabor.
Medieval Greek σπόρτυλον (spórtulon)bor.
Arabic برطيل
Borrowed from Medieval Greek σπόρτυλον (spórtulon), borrowed from Latin sportula.

Probably dissimilated from something, such as a now unknown more concrete signification of بَطَّلَ (baṭṭala, “to render useless; to rescind”), compare for the expected transfix فِطِّيس (fiṭṭīs, “hammer of a blacksmith”), and for the dissimilation بَرْشَم (baršam, “scabbard; hilt”).
g: long stone; oblong stone used to peck millstones
the muzzle of a bear or she-camel
